title: Uniform geometric fibre dimension and torsion cohomological bound
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes with $Y$ quasi-compact [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. There is an integer $e\geq0$ such that every fibre of every base change $f_S:X\times_Y S\to S$ has Krull dimension at most $e$ [def-pc-base-change] [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Moreover, for every separably closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field] [def-pc-separably-closed] and every morphism $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and every torsion abelian étale sheaf $F$ on $X_{\bar y}$, one has $H^q(X_{\bar y},F)=0$ for $q>2e$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Empty fibres are allowed.

source.place: Étale statements, uniform cohomological bound; old split step 2 before the finite-Tor application

proof.text: By the definition of properness, f is of finite type. Apply lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound to f and the quasi-compact base Y. Choose its nonnegative bound e, so dim(X_y) ≤ e for every y in Y. The theorem explicitly allows empty fibres. When Y is empty one may choose e = 0.

Use Scheme.SpecToEquivOfField to write any s:Spec K → Y as Spec(t) followed by Y.fromSpecResidueField y. This is the residue-field factorization of lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality. Pullback pasting identifies X ×_Y Spec K with the base change of f.fiber y along Spec(t). Equip f.fiber y with its canonical residue-field structure map and K with the algebra structure induced by t. The structure map is finite type by base change. Apply the field-extension conjunct of lem-kun-dimension-extension to identify the two dimensions; combine it with the ordinary-fibre bound from step 1. All comparisons are valid for empty fibres.

source.place: Tag 00P3, lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension; schemes.tex Tag 01J9, lemma-characterize-points and following naturality diagram; morphisms.tex Tag 01T4, lemma-base-change-finite-type

proof.text: Let S → Y be any base change and s ∈ S. By the definitions, its fibre is (X ×_Y S) ×_S Spec κ(s). The universal property identifies this with X ×_Y Spec κ(s), using the composite Spec κ(s) → S → Y. Explicitly, a pair of compatible maps to X ×_Y S and Spec κ(s) is exactly a pair of maps to X and Spec κ(s) compatible over Y; the S-component is forced by Spec κ(s) → S. The maps in both directions have identical projections, so their composites are identities. Apply step 2 with L = κ(s). This proves the same bound e for all fibres of all base changes, without any quasi-compactness hypothesis on S.

Fix a separably closed field Ω and a morphism bar y:Spec Ω → Y. Step 2 makes Z = X ×_Y Spec Ω a finite-type Ω-scheme of dimension at most e. Let F be a torsion abelian étale sheaf on Z, i.e. c_F is an isomorphism; by the implication (1)⇒(2) of lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations every local section of F is locally killed by a positive integer, which is the torsion notion used by def-sc-etale-torsion-cd and the three nodes below. By lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd the torsion cohomological dimension of Ω is at most 0. The affine bound new-thm-sc-affine-torsion-cd-bound therefore supplies, for every affine finite-type Ω-scheme of dimension at most e, vanishing of torsion cohomology in degrees greater than e + 0. Feed this affine bound into new-thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd-affine-reduction with K = Ω, d = e and c = 0. Its conclusion is H^q(Z,F) = 0 for every torsion abelian étale sheaf F and q > 2e. These nodes use arbitrary torsion, with no common annihilator or invertibility condition. Their dimension-at-most statements cover the empty scheme as well. Together with step 3 this proves both assertions with the same e. In Lean, the separably closed-field bound and the conclusion use Etale.cohomology of singleFunctor 0, while the affine and affine-to-global bounds use Sheaf.H. Apply the natural isomorphism lem-weil-pbc-sheafH-ext-derived-comparison to convert the field bound to Sheaf.H and to convert the final Sheaf.H vanishing back to the required IsZero statement. AddCommGrpCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton translates zero objects to subsingleton underlying groups. The torsion conversion is exactly the first equivalence of Scheme.isTorsionAbelianSheaf_characterizations.
